faq.q: What is the Ring of Fire?
faq.a: It is a horseshoe-shaped belt about 40,000 km long around the edges of the Pacific Ocean, where many volcanoes and earthquakes happen. It runs from New Zealand through Indonesia, Japan and Alaska, then down the Americas to Chile.
asks: Where is the Ring of Fire?

faq.a: Subduction is when one tectonic plate slides beneath another and sinks into the hot mantle. It is usually a heavy ocean plate, and it makes deep trenches, volcanoes and earthquakes.
asks: What happens when an ocean plate sinks?

faq.q: Which famous volcanoes are on the Ring of Fire?
faq.a: Mount Fuji in Japan, Merapi and Krakatoa in Indonesia, Pinatubo in the Philippines, Mount St Helens in the USA, Popocatépetl in Mexico and Cotopaxi in Ecuador are all on it.
asks: Is Mount Fuji on the Ring of Fire?

faq.q: Why are there so many earthquakes around the Pacific?
faq.a: The plates grind past and under each other, get stuck, and then suddenly slip. About 90 percent of the world’s earthquakes happen along the Ring of Fire.
asks: Why does Japan have so many earthquakes?

faq.q: How fast do tectonic plates move?
faq.a: Most move a few centimetres a year, about as fast as fingernails grow. The Pacific plate is one of the fastest, up to about 10 cm a year.

facts: The Ring of Fire is about 40,000 km long.
About 90% of the world's earthquakes happen along the Ring of Fire (USGS).
About 75% of Earth's volcanoes lie along the Ring of Fire.

quiz.say: What happens to a heavy ocean plate at many edges of the Pacific?
quiz.show: At many Pacific plate edges, a heavy ocean plate…
quiz.why: The heavy ocean plate slides under the other plate: subduction. This makes magma and volcanoes.

wrong.1: Plates are solid rock and cannot float up into the air.
wrong.2: Plates keep moving a few centimetres every year.

quiz.say: Which country sits on the Ring of Fire?
quiz.show: A country on the Ring of Fire is…
quiz.why: Japan lies where several plates meet on the edge of the Pacific.

wrong.1: Egypt is in North Africa, far from the Pacific.
wrong.2: The UK is far from any plate edge, in the Atlantic.
